q: How do I split a footwear factory's emissions across different styles?
title: Footwear factory emissions per pair
short: Total the factory electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25 and generator diesel at 2.68 kg per litre, then split by standard minutes per style rather than pairs, since a boot takes much longer to make than a sandal. State the rule beside each per-pair figure.
audience: Footwear exporters with mixed styles in one factory

p: Dividing by pairs gives every style the same energy. Styles with more operations, such as boots with lasting and stitching, use more machine and lighting time.

ul: Standard minute value (SMV) per style, from industrial engineering data.
Machine hours per line, if lines are dedicated to styles.
Pairs, only when styles are similar.

p: Allocation covers factory energy. Leather, soles and components are added per style from the bill of materials.

example.title: Worked example: pairs versus standard minutes (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Factory total: 52,112 kg CO2 for 40,000 pairs
By pairs: 52,112 / 40,000 = 1.303 kg CO2 per pair
By standard minutes (boots 30, sandals 12; 10,000 boots, 30,000 sandals): boot 2.369 kg, sandal 0.947 kg
example.note: Inputs and minutes are illustrative; use your SMV data.
